chunks: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated from Hamdawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Jabr, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man asked him about a man whom the prayer time overtakes while he is wading in water and cannot reach the land. He said: 'If he is in war or in the path of Allah, let him pray by nodding (indicating with his head). And if he is in trade, it was not appropriate for him to wade in the water until he prays.' I said: 'What should he do?' He said: 'He should make up for it when he exits the water, having missed it.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: by nodding/indicating (a form of prayer while standing)

ai.seo_question: How does a Muslim pray if they are stuck in water when prayer time begins?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between necessity (*darura*) and negligence (*taqsir*) in the performance of prayer. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while those in active jihad or travel may pray by nodding (*i'nam*) in the water due to genuine constraint, a merchant who wades for leisure is considered negligent and must offer a full makeup prayer (*qada*) upon exiting, highlighting the ethical weight of intentional delay.
